tasks.corrected_reference_answer: Postgres copies ANSI unordered SELECT grammar and inserts optional INTO before FROM, retaining common grammar without repeating it (src/sqlfluff/dialects/dialect_postgres.py:1781-1796). Its full SELECT then copies the Postgres unordered grammar and adds later clauses (lines 1799-1815). Reapplying that copy is necessary to incorporate the dialect variant because the existing parent copy is not dynamically rebuilt. Defining a grammar from scratch is permitted; composition reduces duplication, not an enforced inheritance constraint.

tasks.corrected_reference_answer: Vertica full SELECT copies its unordered grammar, inserts TimeseriesClauseSegment among later optional clauses, and replaces terminators so TIMESERIES no longer stops that grammar (src/sqlfluff/dialects/dialect_vertica.py:1954-1969). GREEDY_ONCE_STARTED performs terminator lookahead immediately after the first match, using the resulting boundary for remaining elements (src/sqlfluff/core/parser/grammar/sequence.py:319-328). Removing TIMESERIES from that boundary set allows the later optional clause to consume it.
